Blank completion, contrast clue (including received view then finding)
Blank completion, phrase options (word + preposition, a/an + word)
Most nearly mean, underlined phrase or phrase options

items.passage: Although Allied bombing during World War II devastated dozens of Japanese cities, economists Donald Davis and David Weinstein found that within a generation nearly all of them had regained their prewar positions in the national hierarchy of city sizes. This recovery suggests that the relative populations of Japan’s cities are largely ______ even severe temporary shocks.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: To be impervious to something is to be unaffected by it. The text says Allied bombing “devastated dozens of Japanese cities,” yet “within a generation nearly all of them had regained their prewar positions in the national hierarchy of city sizes.” Even a severe shock, then, did not lastingly change the cities’ relative populations: those populations are largely impervious to such shocks.

A.why_wrong: Contingent on means dependent on. The cities “regained their prewar positions” after the bombing, so their relative populations did not end up depending on the shock.

B.why_wrong: Inured to means hardened to something unpleasant by repeated exposure, as a person grows used to hardship. The text describes one wartime shock and the cities’ return to their earlier ranks, not cities growing accustomed to repeated blows.

D.why_wrong: Germane to means relevant to. The text’s point is that the shocks left the hierarchy of city sizes unchanged in the long run, not that city populations are relevant to the shocks.

band7_moves: concessive frame (Although bombing devastated dozens of cities, ... regained their prewar positions) that hides the direction: the severity invites contingent on
two steps: severe damage plus a full return to the old ranking means the ranking was unaffected in the long run
near-synonym distractor failing on one feature (inured to: hardened by repeated exposure, not unaffected)
all four options past rank 17,000, three past 20,000; rarest distractor germane 57,248

sources.what: NBER working paper 8517 page, Davis and Weinstein, “Bones, Bombs and Break Points: The Geography of Economic Activity” (published AER 2002): the Allied bombing of Japanese cities in WWII treated as a shock to relative city sizes; even large temporary shocks to urban areas have no long-run impact on city size

items.notes: Subject: social science (urban economics). Key letter C. Steps: 2. Raw freq.txt ranks: contingent on 17,762; inured to 21,924; impervious to 20,091; germane to 57,248 (mean log10 4.41). Band-5 guard: clear (key is not the rarest). Concessive frame: yes. “Within a generation” and “nearly all” round the paper’s finding that most cities returned to their prewar relative size; the source abstract states the no-long-run-impact conclusion the item hinges on. Immune to and unaffected by were not offered (each would also fit).

items.passage: Isang Yun, a Korean-born composer who made his later career in West Germany, wrote in the idiom of the European avant-garde, yet his compositions are saturated with the glissandi, vibrato, and elaborate ornamentation of traditional Korean music. His work thus ______ the two traditions: in pieces such as Réak (1966), Korean sonorities are not positioned beside avant-garde techniques but interwoven with them.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: To amalgamate is to combine separate things into a single whole. The text says Yun wrote “in the idiom of the European avant-garde,” yet his compositions “are saturated with” the techniques of “traditional Korean music,” and that in his pieces “Korean sonorities are not positioned beside avant-garde techniques but interwoven with them.” His work therefore merges the two traditions: it amalgamates them.

B.why_wrong: To sequester is to keep something apart or isolated. The text says the Korean sonorities are “interwoven with” the avant-garde techniques, which is the opposite of keeping the traditions apart.

C.why_wrong: To juxtapose is to place things side by side. The text specifies that the Korean sonorities “are not positioned beside avant-garde techniques but interwoven with them,” so the traditions are merged, not simply placed next to each other.

D.why_wrong: To supplant is to take the place of something. Nothing in the text suggests that Yun’s work replaces either tradition; it draws on both at once.

band7_moves: rare Latinate key (amalgamates, rank 69,532) pinned by a clue that describes the merging rather than naming it (not positioned beside ... but interwoven with)
near-synonym distractor failing on one feature (juxtaposes: side by side, not merged)
all four options past rank 28,000; rarest distractor juxtaposes unseen

sources.what: Wikipedia, Isang Yun: Korean-born composer who made his later career in West Germany; with Réak (1966) he introduced the sound idea of Korean ceremonial music into Western avant-garde music; his primary musical concern was the fusion of traditional Korean music through Western avant-garde techniques, using glissandi, vibrati and a very rich vocabulary of ornaments

items.notes: Subject: humanities (music). Key letter A. Steps: 1 (the colon clause restates the key in plain words; band 7 through the option set, as with repudiates and ubiquity). Raw freq.txt ranks: amalgamates 69,532; sequesters 39,965; juxtaposes unseen; supplants 28,305 (mean log10 about 5.0). Band-5 guard: clear (a distractor is rarer than the key). Réak is italic in print. Combines, fuses and blends were not offered (each would also fit); conflates was rejected because its neutral sense (to combine into one) would also fit.

items.passage: Approximately 5.33 million years ago, Atlantic water breached the barrier at Gibraltar and refilled the nearly desiccated Mediterranean. Though the inflow may have begun as a trickle lasting millennia, geoscientist Daniel Garcia-Castellanos and colleagues argue that its principal phase was ______: judging from the channel the floodwaters eroded beneath the strait, 90 percent of the water arrived within two years at most.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Precipitous means sudden and dramatic. The text sets the inflow’s possible start, “a trickle lasting millennia,” against its principal phase, in which “90 percent of the water arrived within two years at most.” After thousands of years of trickling, most of a sea’s worth of water arriving within two years is a sudden, dramatic change: the principal phase was precipitous.

A.recipe: reversal: the trait of the other side of the contrast (ANT)
A.why_wrong: Protracted means drawn out over a long time. That describes the early “trickle lasting millennia,” which the text contrasts with the principal phase, when “90 percent of the water arrived within two years at most.”

B.why_wrong: Sporadic means happening at irregular intervals. The text does not say the water came in separate bursts; it says that nearly all of it arrived within a short span.

C.why_wrong: Imperceptible means too slight to be noticed. Nothing suggests the principal phase was slight; the text stresses that 90 percent of the water that refilled the Mediterranean arrived within two years.

sources.what: PubMed abstract, Garcia-Castellanos et al. 2009 (Nature), Catastrophic flood of the Mediterranean after the Messinian salinity crisis: Atlantic waters refilled the desiccated Mediterranean 5.33 million years ago (Zanclean flood); incisions across the Gibraltar Strait explained as erosion by the flood; although the flood started at low discharges that may have lasted up to several thousand years, 90 per cent of the water was transferred in a few months to two years

items.notes: Subject: natural science (geology). Key letter D. Band 6 (the cell's target): a contrast with an implicit direction (a long trickle against the main phase), a key that paraphrases the source's “extremely abrupt” without echoing the passage, the other side's trait (protracted) as the reversal, and a near miss (sporadic). Raw freq.txt ranks: protracted 18,293; sporadic 39,991; imperceptible 12,942; precipitous 15,420. Sudden, abrupt and rapid were not offered (each would also fit).

items.passage: A 2016 analysis by Alice Popejoy and Stephanie Fullerton found that roughly 80 percent of participants in genome-wide association studies, which scan thousands of genomes for variants associated with disease, were of European descent. Because a variant’s association with a disease can differ in strength from one ancestral population to another, this imbalance may limit how ______ the studies’ findings are.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: As used here, portable means able to be carried over to a different setting and still apply. The text says about 80 percent of participants were “of European descent” and that “a variant’s association with a disease can differ in strength from one ancestral population to another.” Findings drawn mostly from one population may therefore not hold for others, so the imbalance may limit how portable the findings are.

A.why_wrong: Anecdotal means based on scattered personal accounts rather than systematic study. To limit how anecdotal the findings are would make them more solid, but the text presents the imbalance as a reason for caution about the findings, not as a strength.

C.why_wrong: Provisional means tentative. To limit how provisional the findings are would make them more settled, but the text treats the imbalance as a reason for caution about the findings, not as a reason to trust them more.

D.why_wrong: Proprietary means privately owned. Nothing in the text concerns who owns the studies’ findings; it concerns the ancestry of the people studied.

band7_moves: negation hidden in a verb (may limit how ______), as preclude and fail to hide it in the band-7 models
familiar word in a transferred sense (portable: applicable in another setting, not easy to carry)
two steps: a mostly European sample plus links that vary by ancestry means findings may not carry over
distractors from the same academic register (anecdotal, provisional, proprietary), so register gives nothing away

sources.what: PMC full text, Popejoy and Fullerton 2016 (Nature comment), Genomics is failing on diversity: a 2009 analysis found 96% of GWAS participants were of European descent; by 2016 the share not of European descent had risen to nearly 20%; GWAS scan the genomes of thousands of people to find variants associated with disease traits; a variant associated with diabetes may confer a different risk in someone of European ancestry than in someone of African ancestry

items.notes: Subject: natural science (genetics). Key letter B. Steps: 2. Negated frame: hidden (limit how). Transferred-sense key: yes. Raw freq.txt ranks: anecdotal 41,758; portable 20,596; provisional 26,070; proprietary 32,117 (mean log10 about 4.50). Band-5 guard: clear. Hedged to the source: “may limit”. Generalizable, transferable and applicable were not offered (each would also fit); replicable, exhaustive and durable were rejected as arguably defensible (a durable finding can mean one that holds up in new samples).

items.subtype: Blank completion: cause or consequence clue
items.passage: Studying 452 eminent life scientists who died prematurely, Pierre Azoulay and colleagues found that after each death, publications in the scientist’s subfield by researchers outside the deceased star’s circle of collaborators increased by about 9 percent on average. Since that increase followed the star’s death, the authors propose that a living star’s dominance can ______ the entry of outsiders into a field.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: To dampen something is to reduce or hold it down. The text says that after each death, publications by outsiders “increased by about 9 percent,” and that “that increase followed the star’s death.” While the star was alive, then, outsiders entered the field less than they did afterward, so a living star’s dominance can dampen their entry.

B.why_wrong: To foreclose is to rule out entirely. Outsiders’ publications “increased by about 9 percent,” which means outsiders were already publishing in these subfields while the stars were alive; their entry was reduced, not prevented.

C.why_wrong: To galvanize is to spur into action. If a living star spurred outsiders to enter a field, their publications would be expected to fall after the star’s death, not increase.

D.why_wrong: To legitimize is to make acceptable. A star who made outsiders’ entry acceptable would not be followed by a rise in that entry once the star was gone.

band7_moves: cause in a since clause, with a figurative key (dampen) as in stymie and buttress
two steps: an increase after the star's death implies the star's presence held entry down
near-synonym distractor failing on one feature (foreclose: rules out entirely, while a 9 percent increase shows some entry before)
all four options past rank 35,000; two distractors unseen

sources.what: NBER working paper 21788 page, Azoulay, Fons-Rosen and Graff Zivin, “Does Science Advance One Funeral at a Time?” (AER 2019): entry into the subfields of 452 academic life scientists who passed away prematurely; the flow of articles by non-collaborators increases by 8.6% on average after the death; barriers impede entry; star scientists hold on to their position a bit too long

items.notes: Subject: social science (economics of science). Key letter A. Steps: 2. Figurative key: yes. Raw freq.txt ranks: dampen 51,117; foreclose 35,517; galvanize unseen; legitimize unseen. Band-5 guard: clear (two distractors are rarer). 8.6 percent on average, rounded to about 9. Stymie (an official key), inhibit, curb and suppress were not offered (each would also fit).

items.passage: In 2019 amateur astronomer Gennadiy Borisov detected 2I/Borisov, the first comet known to have originated in another star system, using a 0.65-meter telescope that he had designed and constructed himself. His discovery suggests that amateurs, despite lacking the resources of professional observatories, are by no means ______ to the search for interstellar objects.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Superfluous means unnecessary. The text says an amateur, using a telescope “that he had designed and constructed himself,” found “the first comet known to have originated in another star system.” That discovery shows amateurs can contribute to the search even without “the resources of professional observatories,” so they are by no means superfluous to it.

A.why_wrong: Indispensable means absolutely necessary. Saying amateurs are “by no means” indispensable would deny their value, the opposite of what an amateur’s major discovery suggests.

B.why_wrong: Hostile means unfriendly or opposed. Nothing in the text suggests amateurs might oppose the search; the point concerns whether they can contribute to it.

C.why_wrong: Accustomed means used to something. The text describes a single discovery, not whether amateurs are familiar with searching for interstellar objects.

sources.what: Wikipedia, 2I/Borisov: first observed rogue comet and second observed interstellar interloper, discovered on 30 August 2019 by amateur astronomer Gennadiy Borisov at his observatory in Nauchnij, Crimea, using a 0.65 meter telescope he designed and built himself

items.notes: Subject: natural science (astronomy). Key letter D. Negated frame: by no means. Raw freq.txt ranks: indispensable 10,496; hostile 6,320; accustomed 1,599; superfluous 9,923. Irrelevant, unnecessary and dispensable were not offered (each would also fit). ʻOumuamua was an asteroid-like object, so “first comet” follows the source.

items.passage: For The Black Photo Album/Look at Me: 1890–1950, South African photographer Santu Mofokeng assembled studio portraits commissioned by Black working- and middle-class families. Although some of the images were staged, with Victorian-style settings, props, and poses, Mofokeng treats them as ______ how the sitters imagined themselves, since nothing suggests that the sitters were coerced.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Indicative of means showing or pointing to something. The portraits were “commissioned by” the families themselves, and “nothing suggests that the sitters were coerced,” so even the staged settings and poses can be read as choices the sitters accepted. Mofokeng therefore treats the images as indicative of “how the sitters imagined themselves.”

A.why_wrong: Misleading about means giving a false impression of. The staging might seem to make the portraits misleading, but the text says Mofokeng trusts them as evidence because the families commissioned them and “nothing suggests that the sitters were coerced.”

C.why_wrong: Indifferent to means having no interest in. The text gives no reason to think the portraits disregard how the sitters saw themselves; it presents them as made at the families’ request.

D.why_wrong: Critical of means disapproving of. Nothing in the text suggests that Mofokeng or the portraits pass judgment on how the sitters imagined themselves.

sources.what: Publisher description (Steidl, distributed by D.A.P.), Santu Mofokeng: The Black Photo Album, Look at Me: 1890–1950: private photographs that urban black working and middle-class families in South Africa commissioned between 1890 and 1950; painterly, evoking Victorian photography; some are fiction in setting, props, clothing and pose, yet there is no evidence of coercion; the images reveal how these people imagined themselves; Mofokeng analyses their self-image

items.notes: Subject: humanities (photography). Key letter B. Steps: 2 (staged images might seem untrustworthy, but commissioning without coercion makes them evidence of self-image). Raw freq.txt ranks: misleading 17,174; indicative 20,438; indifferent 2,479; critical 3,140. Revealing of, evidence of and a record of were not offered (each would also fit). The title is italic in print.

items.passage: Many psychologists have maintained that self-control depends on a limited resource, so that exercising it on one task leaves people with less for the next, a phenomenon called ego depletion. But when 23 laboratories conducted an identical experiment with more than 2,000 participants for a 2016 report, the effect they measured was ______: too small to be distinguished from zero.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Negligible means so small as to be unimportant. The text explains right after the blank that the measured effect was “too small to be distinguished from zero,” which is what it means for an effect to be negligible.

A.why_wrong: Robust means strong and reliable. An effect “too small to be distinguished from zero” is the opposite of robust.

B.why_wrong: Inconsistent means varying from case to case. The text reports a single combined measurement and says it was “too small to be distinguished from zero”; it describes the effect’s size, not differences among the laboratories.

D.why_wrong: Cumulative means building up over time. Ego depletion is described as one task leaving less for “the next,” but nothing in the text says the 2016 effect grew larger as tasks accumulated.

sources.what: PubMed abstract, Hagger et al. 2016 (Perspectives on Psychological Science), A Multilab Preregistered Replication of the Ego-Depletion Effect: self-control conceptualized as a limited resource that becomes depleted after exertion; 23 laboratories (total N = 2,141) ran a standardized sequential-task protocol; the ego-depletion effect was small with a 95% CI encompassing zero (d = 0.04)

items.notes: Subject: social science (psychology). Key letter C. Raw freq.txt ranks: robust 11,074; inconsistent 12,228; negligible 31,319; cumulative 22,027. Minimal, trivial and insignificant were not offered (each would also fit).

items.subtype: Blank completion: cause or consequence clue
items.passage: At Hatnub, an ancient Egyptian alabaster quarry, archaeologist Yannis Gourdon and colleagues identified a ramp from the reign of Khufu that ascends at an inclination of 20 percent or more, flanked by staircases punctuated with post holes. The researchers believe that fastening a loaded sledge with ropes to wooden posts installed in those holes ______ the hauling, enabling laborers to drag blocks up such a steep incline.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Facilitated means made easier. The text says that tying the sledge to the posts did something to the hauling, “enabling laborers to drag blocks up such a steep incline.” An arrangement that let workers move blocks up a slope of “20 percent or more” made the hauling easier: it facilitated the work.

A.why_wrong: Hindered means made more difficult. The text says the arrangement was “enabling laborers to drag blocks up such a steep incline,” so it helped the hauling rather than obstructing it.

B.why_wrong: Documented means recorded. The posts and ropes were part of how the blocks were moved; nothing in the text suggests they kept a record of the hauling.

C.why_wrong: Standardized means made uniform. The text explains that the arrangement let workers haul blocks up a steep slope; it says nothing about making the hauling the same each time.

sources.what: Wikipedia, Hatnub (citing the 2018 University of Liverpool and IFAO announcement): ramp at the Hatnub alabaster quarry dating to the reign of Khufu; project co-director Yannis Gourdon of IFAO: a central ramp flanked by two staircases with numerous post holes; a sled carrying a stone block, attached with ropes to the wooden posts, let workers pull alabaster blocks up slopes of 20 percent or more

items.notes: Subject: social science (archaeology). Key letter D. Raw freq.txt ranks: hindered 7,465; documented 5,158; standardized unseen; facilitated 20,550. Eased, enabled and aided were not offered (each would also fit).

items.subtype: Blank completion: contrast clue (received view, then finding)
items.passage: Histories of modern design long presented Ludwig Mies van der Rohe as the ______ creator of the Barcelona chair, which debuted at the 1929 International Exposition. Subsequent scholarship has established, however, that the German designer Lilly Reich, his collaborator for more than a decade, co-designed the chair, although introductory textbooks still rarely acknowledge her contribution.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Sole means only. The text contrasts the older histories with later scholarship, which “has established, however,” that Lilly Reich “co-designed the chair.” For that finding to correct the histories, they must have presented Mies as the chair’s only creator: its sole creator.

B.why_wrong: Acclaimed means praised. Mies could be presented as the chair’s acclaimed creator and still have had a co-designer, so the later finding that Reich “co-designed the chair” would not contradict that view, as the word “however” requires.

C.recipe: reversal: the trait of the finding (ANT)
C.why_wrong: Joint means shared. A shared creation is what later scholarship found, since Reich “co-designed the chair”; the older histories that the scholarship corrects did not present Mies that way.

D.why_wrong: Reluctant means unwilling. Nothing in the text suggests that the histories described Mies as hesitant about creating the chair.

sources.what: Wikipedia, Lilly Reich: German designer and close collaborator of Mies van der Rohe from 1925 to 1938; the Barcelona chair made its first appearance at the 1929 Barcelona International Exposition; Reich co-designed the Barcelona chair, Brno chair and Barcelona Pavilion with Mies; her contribution became clear only through later historians' research; she is rarely mentioned in textbooks

items.notes: Subject: humanities (design history). Key letter A. Received view, then finding, with the blank on the received view; joint (the finding's trait) is the reversal. Raw freq.txt ranks: sole 3,423; acclaimed 32,624; joint 6,609; reluctant 6,398. Only, exclusive and single were not offered (each would also fit); principal and original were rejected as arguably compatible with the received view.

items.passage: Plena, a style of music that originated in the San Antón neighborhood of Ponce, Puerto Rico, around 1900, has long been called the “sung newspaper.” The nickname reflects the ______ nature of its lyrics, which usually told of recent local events such as crimes, hurricanes, or the arrival of important visitors.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Topical means dealing with current events. The text says plena lyrics “usually told of recent local events,” which is why the music was called the “sung newspaper.” Lyrics about recent happenings are topical.

A.why_wrong: Repetitive means repeating the same thing again and again. The text says the lyrics reported a variety of recent events, such as “crimes, hurricanes, or the arrival of important visitors,” not that they repeated themselves.

C.why_wrong: Ancient means very old. The lyrics told of “recent local events,” the opposite of ancient subjects.

D.why_wrong: Foreign means from another country. The lyrics told of “local events,” so nothing suggests they were foreign.

sources.what: Wikipedia, Plena: originated in Barrio San Antón, Ponce, Puerto Rico, around 1900; often called the periódico cantado or “sung newspaper”; its lyrics related to current events, such as the arrival of a personage, a crime, a bank moratorium or a hurricane

items.notes: Subject: humanities (music). Key letter B. Raw freq.txt ranks: repetitive unseen (a modern word the old corpus misses); topical 44,337 (common in modern use); ancient 1,340; foreign 2,046. Timely and current were not offered (each would also fit); humorous was rejected because plena is described as satirical.

items.passage: In 2005 microbiologist Gemma Reguera and colleagues found that the hairlike filaments, or pili, of the bacterium Geobacter sulfurreducens are highly ______. The filaments carry electric current and may act as tiny wires, passing electrons from the cell to iron minerals in the surrounding soil.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Conductive means able to carry electricity. The next sentence says the filaments “carry electric current and may act as tiny wires,” so they are highly conductive.

A.why_wrong: Transparent means able to be seen through. The text describes the filaments carrying current, not how they look.

B.why_wrong: Brittle means easily broken. Nothing in the text concerns how strong or fragile the filaments are.

D.why_wrong: Insulated means shielded so that electricity cannot pass. The filaments “carry electric current,” which is the opposite.

sources.what: PubMed abstract, Reguera et al. 2005 (Nature), Extracellular electron transfer via microbial nanowires: Geobacter species reduce Fe(III) oxides; conducting-probe atomic force microscopy showed the pili of G. sulfurreducens were highly conductive; the pili might serve as biological nanowires transferring electrons from the cell surface to Fe(III) oxides

items.notes: Subject: natural science (microbiology). Key letter C. Raw freq.txt ranks: transparent 7,165; brittle 22,307; conductive unseen (a modern technical word); insulated 48,468. Hedged to the source: “may act as tiny wires.”

items.passage: Before November 18, 1883, timekeeping on North American railroads was highly ______: each company chose its own time standard, and the Northern Pacific Railroad alone used seven different time zones along its route. On that date, most railroads in the United States and Canada reset their clocks to a shared system of zones.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Inconsistent means not the same from one case to another. The text says “each company chose its own time standard” and that one railroad “alone used seven different time zones.” Timekeeping that differed from railroad to railroad was inconsistent.

B.why_wrong: Precise means exact. The text is about railroads using different standards from one another, not about how exact any one railroad’s clocks were.

C.why_wrong: Uniform means the same everywhere. Because “each company chose its own time standard,” timekeeping was not uniform until the railroads adopted “a shared system of zones.”

D.why_wrong: Controversial means causing public disagreement. The text describes differing time standards but says nothing about disputes over them.

sources.what: Wikipedia, Standard time: until 1883 each United States railroad chose its own time standards; the Northern Pacific Railroad had seven time zones between St. Paul and its west end; on Sunday, November 18, 1883, all United States and Canadian railroads readjusted their clocks to the new zone system

items.notes: Subject: history (technology and transport). Key letter A. Raw freq.txt ranks: inconsistent 12,228; precise 7,141; uniform 4,122; controversial 33,131. Varied and fragmented were not offered (each would also fit).

items.passage: In 1934 Sierra Leonean choreographer Asadata Dafora staged Kykunkor (The Witch Woman), a successful dance drama built on traditional African music and dance. Dafora is now regarded as a ______ of Black concert dance in the United States, since he was one of the first African artists to bring African drumming to American audiences.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: A pioneer is one of the first people to do something new. The text explains that Dafora “was one of the first African artists to bring African drumming to American audiences,” so he is regarded as a pioneer of Black concert dance in the United States.

A.why_wrong: A critic judges the work of others. The text describes Dafora creating and staging a dance drama, not reviewing other artists’ work.

B.why_wrong: A follower comes after others and imitates them. Dafora was “one of the first” to bring African drumming to American audiences, so he led rather than followed.

C.why_wrong: A sponsor pays for or supports someone else’s project. The text says Dafora staged his own production, not that he funded the work of others.

sources.what: Wikipedia, Asadata Dafora: Sierra Leonean musician, dancer and choreographer; one of the first Africans to introduce African drumming music to the United States, beginning in the early 1930s; in 1934 created Kykunkor (The Witch Woman), a successful production using authentic African music and dance; considered one of the pioneers of black dance in America

items.notes: Subject: humanities (dance). Key letter D. Raw freq.txt ranks: critic 6,418; follower 17,505; sponsor 16,525; pioneer 15,814. Founder and forerunner were not offered (each would also fit). Kykunkor is italic in print.

items.passage:
The following text is from Percy Fitzpatrick’s 1897 short story collection The Outspan: Tales of South Africa. The narrator, a traveler, is waiting in the parlor of a woman’s cottage while she prepares a letter.

I sat waiting while the minutes passed, and not a sound <u>broke</u> the perfect silence in the house. Everything was so still that it seemed as if there could be no one within miles of me.
items.stem: As used in the text, what does the word “broke” most nearly mean?
items.explanation: In the text, “not a sound broke the perfect silence in the house,” and the next sentence adds, “Everything was so still that it seemed as if there could be no one within miles of me.” No sound cut into the silence, so “broke” most nearly means interrupted.

A.why_wrong: Broke can mean damaged, as when someone breaks a cup, but a sound does not physically damage silence; the text means that no sound cut into the quiet.

B.why_wrong: Broke can mean revealed, as in breaking news, but the text is not about information being made known; it says the house stayed perfectly quiet.

D.why_wrong: Broke can mean tamed, as when a horse is broken, but nothing in the text is being trained; the sentence describes a silence that no sound disturbed.

sources.what: Project Gutenberg eBook 37260, Percy Fitzpatrick, The Outspan: Tales of South Africa (edition dated 1897), chapter “Induna Nairn”: the excerpt copied exactly

items.notes: Subject: literature (short story). Key letter C. The context line paraphrases the scene: the woman leaves the narrator in her parlor and returns with a letter for him to carry. Excerpt copied exactly from the Gutenberg text. Raw freq.txt ranks: damaged 6,756; revealed 2,383; interrupted 1,362; tamed 7,226. Disturbed was not offered (it would also fit).

items.passage:
The following text is from Walter F. White’s 1924 novel The Fire in the Flint. Judge Stevenson is an elderly lawyer.

Skin reddened by exposure to sun and wind, bushy eyebrows from under which gleamed fiery eyes that could shift in an instant from twinkling good humour to flashing indignation or anger, thin nose and ample mouth, his face was one that would <u>command</u> respect or at least attention in almost any gathering.
items.stem: As used in the text, what does the word “command” most nearly mean?
items.explanation: The text says the judge’s striking face “would command respect or at least attention in almost any gathering.” A face cannot give orders; it draws respect or attention from the people who see it. In this context, “command” most nearly means attract.

A.why_wrong: Command can mean order, as when an officer commands troops to march, but a face cannot order people to feel respect; the text means the face draws respect from others.

C.why_wrong: Command can mean to overlook, as when a hilltop commands a view of a valley, but the text is not about a view; it is about the respect or “attention” the judge’s face draws.

D.why_wrong: Command can mean lead, as when a general commands an army, but the object here is “respect or at least attention,” which a face draws rather than leads.

items.passage:
The following text is adapted from Mary McNeil Fenollosa’s 1906 novel The Dragon Painter. The text describes the garden of Kano, an elderly painter in Japan.

A stone wall upheld [the garden’s] front edge from the narrow street; and on top of this wall stiff hedges grew. In one corner, however, a hillock had been <u>raised</u>, a “Moon Viewing Place,” such as poets and artists have always found necessary.
items.stem: As used in the text, what does the word “raised” most nearly mean?
items.explanation: The text says that in one corner of the garden “a hillock had been raised,” a small hill made as a “Moon Viewing Place.” A hillock that someone heaped up in a garden has been built, so “raised” most nearly means built.

B.why_wrong: Raised can mean mentioned, as when someone raises a question, but a hillock in a garden is a physical feature that was made, not a topic brought up in conversation.

C.why_wrong: Raised can mean increased, as when a store raises its prices, but nothing in the garden is being made larger in amount; the text says a small hill was made in one corner.

D.why_wrong: Raised can mean collected, as when someone raises money, but the text describes a hill made in the garden, not something gathered from others.

sources.what: Project Gutenberg eBook 22884, The Dragon Painter, title page by Mary McNeil Fenollosa (Little, Brown, and Company, published October 1906); Wikipedia lists The Dragon Painter (1906) as published under her own name: the excerpt copied from the description of Kano’s garden

items.notes: Subject: literature (novel). Key letter A. Adapted: the passage begins with the novel’s second sentence about the garden, with [the garden’s] replacing “its”; the rest copied exactly. Gutenberg lists the author by her earlier pen name Sidney McCall, but this book appeared under her own name. Raw freq.txt ranks: built 1,425; mentioned 1,758; increased 2,145; collected 4,450. Made and formed were not offered (each would also fit); lifted was rejected as too close to the core sense, and reared because it can itself mean erected.

items.passage: Engineer Ophelia Bolmin and colleagues have investigated how click beetles accomplish their remarkable jumps. Because the insects’ muscles cannot release energy quickly enough on their own, each jump is ______ a spring-and-latch mechanism: the beetle bends its body at a hinge, secures the position with a latch, and then unbends extremely rapidly, producing an audible click.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Powered by means driven by. The text says the beetles’ muscles “cannot release energy quickly enough on their own,” and then describes the beetle storing its bent position with a latch and unbending “extremely rapidly.” The energy for each jump therefore comes from the spring-and-latch mechanism: the jump is powered by it.

A.why_wrong: Slowed by means made slower by. The mechanism lets the beetle unbend “extremely rapidly,” so it speeds the jump rather than slowing it.

B.why_wrong: Timed by means measured or scheduled by. The text explains where the energy for the jump comes from, not how the jump is timed.

C.why_wrong: Named for means given a name in honor of. The beetles produce a click, but the text does not say the jump is named for the mechanism.

sources.what: PubMed abstract, Bolmin et al. 2021 (PNAS), Nonlinear elasticity and damping govern ultrafast dynamics in click beetles: many small animals use springs and latches to overcome the power limits of their muscles; click beetles use springs and latches to bend their bodies at the thoracic hinge and then unbend extremely quickly, resulting in a clicking motion and, when unconstrained, a jump; phases of latching, loading and energy release

items.notes: Subject: natural science (biomechanics). Key letter D. Raw freq.txt ranks, printed forms: slowed 17,202; timed 13,538; named 1,949; powered 41,465 (each verb’s base form is common). Driven by and fueled by were not offered (each would also fit).

items.passage: Composer Julia Perry received rigorous training in European classical music at Westminster Choir College and the Juilliard School. Even so, several of her early compositions are ______ African American music: her 1951 pieces Free at Last and I’m a Poor Li’l Orphan, for instance, draw on Black spirituals.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Rooted in means having origins in. The text gives two of Perry’s 1951 pieces as examples of works that “draw on Black spirituals,” so several of her early compositions are rooted in African American music.

A.why_wrong: Unknown to means not known by. The text says nothing about whether audiences of African American music knew Perry’s works; it says the works “draw on Black spirituals.”

B.why_wrong: Opposed to means against. Works that “draw on Black spirituals” embrace African American music rather than oppose it.

D.why_wrong: Required for means needed in order to have something. Nothing in the text suggests that African American music needed Perry’s compositions.

sources.what: Wikipedia, Julia Perry: American composer who combined European classical and neo-classical training with her African-American heritage; studied at Westminster Choir College (1943–1948) and the Juilliard School; some early compositions heavily influenced by African-American music; Free at Last and I’m a Poor Li’l Orphan (published 1951) showcased her incorporation of black spiritual music

items.notes: Subject: humanities (music). Key letter C. Raw freq.txt ranks: unknown 1,536; opposed 6,009; rooted 5,207; required 2,039. Influenced by, inspired by and grounded in were not offered (each would also fit). Titles italic in print.

items.passage: In 1946 an earthquake near Alaska’s Aleutian Islands generated a tsunami that killed more than 170 people in Hawaii, where authorities had no means of warning residents about approaching waves. The catastrophe prompted the United States to ______ a warning system headquartered in Honolulu, which became operational in 1948 and is now known as the Pacific Tsunami Warning Center.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: To establish something is to set it up. Because the 1946 tsunami struck when authorities “had no means of warning residents,” the disaster led the United States to create a warning system, one that “became operational in 1948.” The country established it.

A.why_wrong: To abandon is to give up. The system “became operational in 1948” and still exists as the Pacific Tsunami Warning Center, so it was not abandoned.

C.why_wrong: To postpone is to delay. The text presents the disaster as the reason a warning system was created, not as a reason to delay one.

D.why_wrong: To imitate is to copy. Since there had been “no means of warning residents,” the text gives no earlier system that the new one copied.

sources.what: Wikipedia, Pacific Tsunami Warning Center: until the late 1940s the United States had no way to warn the public about tsunamis; after the 1946 Aleutian Islands earthquake, whose tsunami killed more than 170 people in Hawaii, a warning plan was devised; the facility became operational in 1948 as the Seismic Sea Wave Warning System, headquartered in Honolulu, later renamed the Pacific Tsunami Warning Center

items.notes: Subject: history (science and public safety). Key letter B. Raw freq.txt ranks: abandon 5,885; establish 6,627; postpone 12,469; imitate 10,889. Create and develop were not offered (each would also fit).

items.passage: Romuald Hazoumè, an artist from Benin, works only with ______ materials. Since the mid-1980s, for example, he has turned discarded gasoline containers into masks resembling those used in traditional African ceremonies, sending what he calls the refuse of consumer society back to the West.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Recycled materials are ones that have been used before and are put to a new use. The example given is that Hazoumè “has turned discarded gasoline containers into masks,” giving thrown-away objects a second life, so he works only with recycled materials.

B.why_wrong: Costly means expensive. The example is “discarded gasoline containers,” which are thrown away, not costly.

C.why_wrong: Fragile means easily broken. The text says nothing about how delicate Hazoumè’s materials are; it stresses that they were discarded.

D.why_wrong: Unused means new and never used before. The containers in the example were “discarded,” having already been used.

sources.what: Wikipedia, Romuald Hazoumè: artist from the Republic of Bénin who only uses recycled materials; mask series begun in the mid-1980s, made from discarded gasoline canisters and resembling those used in traditional African culture and ceremonies; his explanation: “I send back to the West that which belongs to them, that is to say, the refuse of consumer society that invades us every day”

items.notes: Subject: humanities (art). Key letter A. Raw freq.txt ranks: recycled 60,878 (common in modern use); costly 1,508; fragile 9,404; unused 11,055. Discarded, salvaged and secondhand were not offered (each would also fit).

items.passage: Whip spiders are nocturnal predators that can navigate back to their shelters even after being displaced 10 meters away. In a 2017 experiment, Verner Bingman and colleagues found that vision is not ______ to this homing ability: spiders whose eyesight was blocked generally returned home, whereas those whose long, antenna-like front legs were impaired lost their way entirely.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Essential means necessary. The text explains that “spiders whose eyesight was blocked generally returned home,” so the spiders could find their way without seeing. Vision is therefore not essential to their homing ability.

A.why_wrong: Comparable means similar or able to be likened. The text does not compare vision with the spiders’ homing ability; it reports whether the spiders need vision to get home.

B.why_wrong: Irrelevant means having no bearing on something. Saying vision is not irrelevant would mean it matters for homing, but spiders “whose eyesight was blocked generally returned home.”

D.why_wrong: Unknown means not known. The text is about whether the spiders need vision to get home, not about whether vision is known to them.

sources.what: PubMed abstract, Bingman et al. 2017 (Journal of Experimental Biology), Importance of the antenniform legs, but not vision, for homing by the neotropical whip spider Paraphrynus laevifrons: nocturnal arthropods displaced 10 m from their refuge; vision-deprived individuals were generally successful in returning home, while those with the tips of the antenniform legs compromised lost all navigational ability

items.notes: Subject: natural science (animal behavior). Key letter C. Negated frame: is not. Raw freq.txt ranks: comparable 16,254; irrelevant 14,569; essential 5,974; unknown 1,536. Necessary, crucial and required were not offered (each would also fit); useful and harmful were rejected (not useful and not harmful would be arguable). Published 2017 (online December 2016).

items.passage: Although many animals flee forest fires, jewel beetles of the genus Melanophila are not ______ by them: the beetles fly toward burning forests, since their larvae can develop only in trees killed by fire. Researchers in Germany have studied the infrared-sensing organs that allow the beetles to detect fires, possibly from many kilometers away.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: To be repelled by something is to be driven away by it. Unlike animals that “flee forest fires,” these beetles “fly toward burning forests,” so they are not repelled by fires.

A.why_wrong: Attracted means drawn toward. Saying the beetles are not attracted by fires would contradict the statement that they “fly toward burning forests.”

C.why_wrong: Outnumbered means exceeded in number. The text says nothing about how many beetles or fires there are.

D.why_wrong: Illuminated means lit up. Fires give off light, but the text contrasts beetles that approach fires with animals that flee them; it does not concern whether fires light up the beetles.

sources.what: PubMed abstract, Schneider, Schmitz and Schmitz 2015 (Frontiers in Physiology), Concept of an Active Amplification Mechanism in the Infrared Organ of Pyrophilous Melanophila Beetles: jewel beetles of the genus Melanophila possess infrared organs used for forest fire detection because their larvae can only develop in fire-killed trees; reports suggest detection of large fires from very long distances, with measured sensitivity allowing detection up to 12 km

items.notes: Subject: natural science (insect sensing). Key letter B. Negated frame: are not. Raw freq.txt ranks: attracted 2,958; repelled 10,635; outnumbered 23,321; illuminated 6,881. Deterred and frightened were not offered (each would also fit). The authors work at the University of Bonn.
